changes.why: v0.3.0 makes partition a split by a predicate (Haskell's partition), returning [passing, failing]; its key-grouping body became groupBy's: partition(x => x % 2, [0, 1, 2, 3]) went from {0: [0, 2], 1: [1, 3]} to [[1, 3], [0, 2]], so fn: T -> string became pred: T -> bool and the result a pair
knock-on of partition: v0.3.0 makes groupBy its own function with partition's old body instead of an alias of partition; the revealed body no longer calls List.partition, same results
v0.3.0 moves the K alias from tap (not portable) to always: aliasFor('always').is('constant').and('K')
new in v0.3.0: R.ap(fns, vs), each function mapped over vs and the results concatenated
new in v0.3.0: R.chain(f, list) is unnest(map(f, list))
new in v0.3.0: R.unnest flattens one level (makeFlat(false))
new in v0.3.0: R.zipObj(keys, values), a later duplicate key wins
new in v0.3.0: R.fromPairs(pairs), a later duplicate key wins
new in v0.3.0: R.mathMod(m, p) is ((m % p) + p) % p, NaN unless m is an integer >= 1 and p a nonzero integer
